# Music

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Audio` · class

```csharp
public sealed class Music : IContent
```

Types: [`IContent`](IContent.md)

A long piece of audio streamed as it plays, for background music. Load it from content; the content service owns it, so release it with `Content.UnloadAsync`.

## Properties

### Duration

```csharp
public TimeSpan Duration { get; }
```

Gets the total duration of this music track. The value is precomputed by the content pipeline when available; otherwise it is determined by the platform codec at load time.

### IsDisposed

```csharp
public bool IsDisposed { get; }
```

Whether it has been released.

### IsPaused

```csharp
public bool IsPaused { get; }
```

Whether the music is paused, from the moment [`Pause`](#pause) is called on music that's playing, even if it was still loading. [`Resume`](#resume) carries on, and [`Play`](#play) or [`Stop`](#stop) ends it.

Music paused while still loading finishes loading, and doesn't start until [`Resume`](#resume). If it can't be loaded, this becomes `false`.

### IsPlaying

```csharp
public bool IsPlaying { get; }
```

Whether the music is playing, from the moment [`Play`](#play) or [`Resume`](#resume) is called. Becomes `false` when playback reaches the end, on [`Stop`](#stop) and [`Pause`](#pause), and when the music can't be loaded.

It says what was asked for, not that sound is coming out yet: music that's still loading, or waiting for the player's first tap in a browser, is playing already, and starts by itself. To know it's ready, await [`PrepareAsync`](#prepareasync).

The system can refuse to play, as Android does while another app holds the audio, and then it stays `false`. It's cheap on every platform, so it's safe to read each frame.

## Methods

### Pause

```csharp
public void Pause()
```

Pauses playback of this music, retaining all of its buffers and its playback position.

A subsequent [`Resume`](#resume) carries on exactly where playback left off. Pausing never releases memory; use [`Stop`](#stop) for that.

Returns immediately, never blocks the calling thread, and is safe to call on music that is not playing or has been disposed. Pausing music that is still loading to play keeps it from starting until [`Resume`](#resume), and [`IsPaused`](#ispaused) is `true` at once.

### Play

```csharp
public void Play(TimeSpan? start = default, TimeSpan? end = default, TimeSpan? loopPoint = null, bool loop = false)
```

Starts this music playing.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `start` | The time offset within the music to start playback, or if not specified, the start of the music. |
| `end` | The time offset within the music to end playback, or if not specified, the end of the music. |
| `loopPoint` | The time offset within the music to loop back to, or if not specified, the start of the music. |
| `loop` | `true` if playback should loop back to `loopPoint` when `end` is reached, or `false` if playback should stop there. |

Returns immediately and never blocks the calling thread. The fetch, decode, and buffer allocation it requires, unless [`PrepareAsync`](#prepareasync) did them, are performed on a background thread and playback begins as soon as they complete. [`IsPlaying`](#isplaying) is `true` from this call.

Starts from the beginning of the range, whatever the music was doing, as a voice does: [`Resume`](#resume) carries on from a pause. If it's already loading to play, that carries on, and it starts once.

Playing retains the music's buffers until [`Stop`](#stop) is called or playback reaches its natural end. On music that has been disposed, it does nothing.

### PrepareAsync

```csharp
public Task PrepareAsync(TimeSpan? start = default, TimeSpan? end = default, TimeSpan? loopPoint = null, bool loop = false)
```

Primes this music for playback: performs the fetch, buffer, decode, and seek work that [`Play`](#play) would otherwise incur on demand, without producing any audio. A subsequent [`Play`](#play) with the same parameters then starts with minimal latency; with others, it prepares again for those.

**Returns:** A task that completes when the music is ready to start at once (immediately when its buffers are already resident).

Trades memory for latency: the music holds its decode and playback buffers from the moment this is called until [`Unprepare`](#unprepare) releases them, instead of only for the duration of playback. The default (never calling this) keeps music optimized for low memory overhead.

All of the work happens on a background thread. This method does not block the calling thread, and awaiting the returned task is optional: [`Play`](#play) may be called at any point before, during, or after preparation and behaves correctly in every case.

Safe to call repeatedly and in any order relative to [`Play`](#play), [`Pause`](#pause), and [`Stop`](#stop). Preparing music that is already prepared for the same range, playing, or paused simply takes the retain and completes. On music that has been disposed, it does nothing.

### Resume

```csharp
public void Resume()
```

Carries on from where [`Pause`](#pause) stopped, with the range and looping it was playing with, or starts it if it was paused while still loading. Does nothing unless [`IsPaused`](#ispaused).

### Stop

```csharp
public void Stop()
```

Stops playback of this music and releases the retain taken by [`Play`](#play).

If [`PrepareAsync`](#prepareasync) still holds a retain, the buffers stay resident and the music stays prepared, so the next [`Play`](#play) is still latency-free. Otherwise the buffers are released on a background thread.

Returns immediately, never blocks the calling thread, and is safe to call on music that is not playing or has been disposed.

### Unprepare

```csharp
public void Unprepare()
```

Releases the retain taken by [`PrepareAsync`](#prepareasync), returning the music to its default low-memory behavior.

Does not stop or interrupt playback. If the music is currently playing or paused, its buffers stay resident and are freed by the eventual [`Stop`](#stop) (or by playback reaching its natural end). Otherwise they are freed on a background thread.

Returns immediately, never blocks the calling thread, and is safe to call repeatedly, in any order, and on music that was never prepared or has been disposed.
